questions.question: Solve √(3x+1) = x − 3 in full, showing why one candidate is rejected and where the marks are paid.
questions.expected_answer: Square both sides: 3x + 1 = x² − 6x + 9, so x² − 9x + 8 = 0, giving (x−8)(x−1) = 0 and candidates x = 8 or x = 1. Test both in the original: x = 8 gives √25 = 5 = 8 − 3, valid; x = 1 gives √4 = 2 but 1 − 3 = −2, rejected since a square root is never negative. Marks: squaring line, standard form, factorising, and the vetting with the stated rejection.

questions.question: For f(x) = x³ + 3x² − 4, give the intercepts, turning points and point of inflection, and describe the shape of the sketch.
questions.expected_answer: Factorise: f(x) = (x−1)(x+2)². X-intercepts at x = 1 (cut) and x = −2 (touch, double root); y-intercept −4. f'(x) = 3x² + 6x = 3x(x+2) = 0 at x = −2 and x = 0: local maximum (−2; 0) on the axis, local minimum (0; −4). Inflection at (−1; −2), midway between the turning points. Shape: rises to touch the axis at −2, dips to the minimum at (0; −4), then rises through (1; 0).

questions.question: Name the five donations on the donation list and the single habit that prevents all of them.
questions.expected_answer: 1) Rounding too early — round once, at the end. 2) The unchecked surd answer — substitute each candidate back. 3) The missing second answer — quadratics give two roots, systems give two pairs. 4) Finance without a timeline — sketch months and payments. 5) Calculus notation — keep the limit symbol until h goes to nought. The collecting habit: one check per answer that costs one line (substitute back, multiply back, count again, test a value).
